### `src/resource/texture.rs` | **Строк:** 537

```rust
//! Texture loading and GPU upload utilities.
//!
//! Uploads use **256-byte-aligned staging rows** (wgpu requirement) and
//! generate a full **mipmap chain** via successive blit render passes, so
//! distant surfaces stop shimmering.

use std::collections::HashMap;
use std::sync::{Arc, LazyLock};

use parking_lot::Mutex;

/// A GPU texture with its view and sampler, ready to be bound in a shader.
pub struct Texture {
    pub texture: wgpu::Texture,
    pub view: wgpu::TextureView,
    pub sampler: wgpu::Sampler,
    pub width: u32,
    pub height: u32,
    /// Total mip levels generated for this texture.
    pub mip_levels: u32,
}

impl Texture {
    /// Decodes image bytes (PNG, JPEG, etc.) and uploads the result to the GPU.
    ///
    /// * `format` — can be `Rgba8UnormSrgb` (default for albedo) or `Rgba8Unorm` (for normals/MR).
    pub fn from_bytes(
        device: &wgpu::Device,
        queue: &wgpu::Queue,
        bytes: &[u8],
        label: &str,
        format: wgpu::TextureFormat,
    ) -> Result<Self, image::ImageError> {
        let img = image::load_from_memory(bytes)?;
        Self::from_image(device, queue, &img, label, format)
    }

    /// Creates a texture from a DynamicImage (with mipmaps).
    ///
    /// For `Rgba8Unorm` labels containing `"normal"` (case-insensitive), mip
    /// levels are built with Toksvig filtering and roughness delta in alpha.
    pub fn from_image(
        device: &wgpu::Device,
        queue: &wgpu::Queue,
        img: &image::DynamicImage,
        label: &str,
        format: wgpu::TextureFormat,
    ) -> Result<Self, image::ImageError> {
        let rgba = img.to_rgba8();
        let (width, height) = rgba.dimensions();

        let is_normal = format == wgpu::TextureFormat::Rgba8Unorm
            && label.to_ascii_lowercase().contains("normal");

        if is_normal {
            return Ok(Self::upload_normal_toksvig(
                device,
                queue,
                width,
                height,
                rgba.as_raw(),
                label,
            ));
        }

        Ok(Self::upload_2d(
            device,
            queue,
            width,
            height,
            format,
            bytemuck::cast_slice(rgba.as_raw()),
            4,
            label,
        ))
    }

    /// Upload an RGBA8 normal map with Toksvig-aware CPU mip chain.
    pub fn upload_normal_toksvig(
        device: &wgpu::Device,
        queue: &wgpu::Queue,
        width: u32,
        height: u32,
        rgba: &[u8],
        label: &str,
    ) -> Self {
        const MAX_DELTA: f32 = 0.5;
        let mips = crate::resource::toksvig::build_normal_mip_chain_toksvig(
            width, height, rgba, MAX_DELTA,
        );
        let mip_levels = mips.len() as u32;
        let format = wgpu::TextureFormat::Rgba8Unorm;

        let size = wgpu::Extent3d {
            width,
            height,
            depth_or_array_layers: 1,
        };
        let texture = device.create_texture(&wgpu::TextureDescriptor {
            label: Some(label),
            size,
            mip_level_count: mip_levels,
            sample_count: 1,
            dimension: wgpu::TextureDimension::D2,
            format,
            usage: wgpu::TextureUsages::TEXTURE_BINDING | wgpu::TextureUsages::COPY_DST,
            view_formats: &[],
        });

        let mut mip_w = width;
        let mut mip_h = height;
        for (level, data) in mips.iter().enumerate() {
            let unpadded_bpr = (mip_w as usize) * 4;
            let bytes_per_row = align256(unpadded_bpr as u32);
            let extent = wgpu::Extent3d {
                width: mip_w,
                height: mip_h,
                depth_or_array_layers: 1,
            };
            if bytes_per_row as usize == unpadded_bpr {
                queue.write_texture(
                    wgpu::ImageCopyTexture {
                        texture: &texture,
                        mip_level: level as u32,
                        origin: wgpu::Origin3d::ZERO,
                        aspect: wgpu::TextureAspect::All,
                    },
                    data,
                    wgpu::ImageDataLayout {
                        offset: 0,
                        bytes_per_row: Some(bytes_per_row),
                        rows_per_image: Some(mip_h),
                    },
                    extent,
                );
            } else {
                let mut padded = vec![0u8; bytes_per_row as usize * mip_h as usize];
                for row in 0..mip_h as usize {
                    let src = row * unpadded_bpr;
                    let dst = row * bytes_per_row as usize;
                    padded[dst..dst + unpadded_bpr]
                        .copy_from_slice(&data[src..src + unpadded_bpr]);
                }
                queue.write_texture(
                    wgpu::ImageCopyTexture {
                        texture: &texture,
                        mip_level: level as u32,
                        origin: wgpu::Origin3d::ZERO,
                        aspect: wgpu::TextureAspect::All,
                    },
                    &padded,
                    wgpu::ImageDataLayout {
                        offset: 0,
                        bytes_per_row: Some(bytes_per_row),
                        rows_per_image: Some(mip_h),
                    },
                    extent,
                );
            }
            mip_w = (mip_w / 2).max(1);
            mip_h = (mip_h / 2).max(1);
        }

        let view = texture.create_view(&wgpu::TextureViewDescriptor::default());
        let sampler = device.create_sampler(&wgpu::SamplerDescriptor {
            label: Some(&format!("{label}_sampler")),
            address_mode_u: wgpu::AddressMode::Repeat,
            address_mode_v: wgpu::AddressMode::Repeat,
            address_mode_w: wgpu::AddressMode::Repeat,
            mag_filter: wgpu::FilterMode::Linear,
            min_filter: wgpu::FilterMode::Linear,
            mipmap_filter: wgpu::FilterMode::Linear,
            ..Default::default()
        });

        Self {
            texture,
            view,
            sampler,
            width,
            height,
            mip_levels,
        }
    }

    /// Loads an HDR (Radiance) image and uploads it as Rgba16Float (filterable).
    pub fn from_hdr_bytes(
        device: &wgpu::Device,
        queue: &wgpu::Queue,
        bytes: &[u8],
        label: &str,
    ) -> Result<Self, image::ImageError> {
        let decoder = image::codecs::hdr::HdrDecoder::new(bytes)?;
        let metadata = decoder.metadata();
        let (width, height) = (metadata.width, metadata.height);
        let pixels = decoder.read_image_hdr()?;

        // Convert Rgb<f32> to RGBA f16 packed as u16.
        let mut data: Vec<u16> = Vec::with_capacity(width as usize * height as usize * 4);
        for pix in pixels {
            data.push(half::f16::from_f32(pix[0]).to_bits());
            data.push(half::f16::from_f32(pix[1]).to_bits());
            data.push(half::f16::from_f32(pix[2]).to_bits());
            data.push(half::f16::from_f32(1.0).to_bits());
        }

        Ok(Self::upload_2d(
            device,
            queue,
            width,
            height,
            wgpu::TextureFormat::Rgba16Float,
            bytemuck::cast_slice(&data),
            2,
            label,
        ))
    }

    /// Core upload path: padded staging copy + mip chain + default sampler.
    ///
    /// `bytes_per_pixel` is 4 for both Rgba8* and Rgba16Float.
    #[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
    pub fn upload_2d(
        device: &wgpu::Device,
        queue: &wgpu::Queue,
        width: u32,
        height: u32,
        format: wgpu::TextureFormat,
        data: &[u8],
        bytes_per_pixel: usize,
        label: &str,
    ) -> Self {
        let mip_levels = width.max(height).max(1).ilog2() + 1;

        let size = wgpu::Extent3d {
            width,
            height,
            depth_or_array_layers: 1,
        };

        let texture = device.create_texture(&wgpu::TextureDescriptor {
            label: Some(label),
            size,
            mip_level_count: mip_levels,
            sample_count: 1,
            dimension: wgpu::TextureDimension::D2,
            format,
            // RENDER_ATTACHMENT is required by the blit-based
            // mip generation (no copy ops needed).
            usage: wgpu::TextureUsages::TEXTURE_BINDING
                | wgpu::TextureUsages::COPY_DST
                | wgpu::TextureUsages::RENDER_ATTACHMENT,
            view_formats: &[],
        });

        // ── Padded staging upload (bytes_per_row must be 256-aligned) ──
        let unpadded_bpr = width as usize * bytes_per_pixel;
        let bytes_per_row = align256(unpadded_bpr as u32);
        if bytes_per_row as usize == unpadded_bpr {
            queue.write_texture(
                wgpu::ImageCopyTexture {
                    texture: &texture,
                    mip_level: 0,
                    origin: wgpu::Origin3d::ZERO,
                    aspect: wgpu::TextureAspect::All,
                },
                data,
                wgpu::ImageDataLayout {
                    offset: 0,
                    bytes_per_row: Some(bytes_per_row as u32 as _),
                    rows_per_image: Some(height),
                },
                size,
            );
        } else {
            // Copy row-by-row into a padded staging buffer.
            let h = height as usize;
            let row_len = unpadded_bpr;
            let mut padded = vec![0u8; bytes_per_row as usize * h];
            for row in 0..h {
                padded[row * bytes_per_row as usize..row * bytes_per_row as usize + row_len]
                    .copy_from_slice(&data[row * row_len..(row + 1) * row_len]);
            }
            queue.write_texture(
                wgpu::ImageCopyTexture {
                    texture: &texture,
                    mip_level: 0,
                    origin: wgpu::Origin3d::ZERO,
                    aspect: wgpu::TextureAspect::All,
                },
                &padded,
                wgpu::ImageDataLayout {
                    offset: 0,
                    bytes_per_row: Some(bytes_per_row as u32 as _),
                    rows_per_image: Some(height),
                },
                size,
            );
        }

        // ── Mip chain via successive blit passes ──
        if mip_levels > 1 {
            generate_mipmaps(device, queue, &texture, mip_levels, format);
        }

        let view = texture.create_view(&wgpu::TextureViewDescriptor::default());
        let sampler = device.create_sampler(&wgpu::SamplerDescriptor {
            label: Some(&format!("{label}_sampler")),
            address_mode_u: wgpu::AddressMode::Repeat,
            address_mode_v: wgpu::AddressMode::Repeat,
            address_mode_w: wgpu::AddressMode::Repeat,
            mag_filter: wgpu::FilterMode::Linear,
            min_filter: wgpu::FilterMode::Linear,
            mipmap_filter: wgpu::FilterMode::Linear,
            ..Default::default()
        });

        Self {
            texture,
            view,
            sampler,
            width,
            height,
            mip_levels,
        }
    }

    /// Creates a solid-color 1×1 texture without any PNG round-tripping.
    pub fn solid_1x1(
        device: &wgpu::Device,
        queue: &wgpu::Queue,
        color: [u8; 4],
        label: &str,
        format: wgpu::TextureFormat,
    ) -> Self {
        Self::upload_2d(device, queue, 1, 1, format, &color, 4, label)
    }

    /// Creates a 1×1 white texture (fallback for materials without a texture).
    pub fn white_1x1(device: &wgpu::Device, queue: &wgpu::Queue) -> Self {
        Self::solid_1x1(device, queue, [255, 255, 255, 255], "white_1x1", wgpu::TextureFormat::Rgba8UnormSrgb)
    }

    /// Creates a 1×1 flat normal map (0.5, 0.5, 1.0 -> [128, 128, 255]).
    pub fn normal_1x1(device: &wgpu::Device, queue: &wgpu::Queue) -> Self {
        Self::solid_1x1(device, queue, [128, 128, 255, 255], "normal_1x1", wgpu::TextureFormat::Rgba8Unorm)
    }

    /// Creates a 1×1 metallic-roughness map (Metallic=0, Roughness=1.0 -> [255, 255, 0, 255]).
    pub fn mr_1x1(device: &wgpu::Device, queue: &wgpu::Queue) -> Self {
        Self::solid_1x1(device, queue, [255, 255, 0, 255], "mr_1x1", wgpu::TextureFormat::Rgba8Unorm)
    }
}

/// Rounds a byte count up to the next multiple of 256 (wgpu alignment).
fn align256(v: u32) -> u32 {
    v.div_ceil(256) * 256
}

/// The WGSL source used for downsampling each mip level.
///
/// UV is derived from the fullscreen-triangle NDC positions in the vertex
/// shader, so it maps exactly onto whatever framebuffer the pass targets —
/// no target-dimension uniform required.
const BLIT_SHADER_SRC: &str = r#"
struct VOut {
    @builtin(position) pos: vec4<f32>,
    @location(0) uv: vec2<f32>,
};
struct Out { @location(0) color: vec4<f32> };

@vertex fn vs(@builtin(vertex_index) vi: u32) -> VOut {
    var p = array<vec2<f32>, 3>(vec2(-1.0, -3.0), vec2(-3.0, 1.0), vec2(3.0, 1.0));
    var o: VOut;
    o.pos = vec4(p[vi], 0.0, 1.0);
    // NDC -> UV (y flipped for framebuffer orientation); oversized triangle
    // covers every pixel, sampler clamp handles the overhang.
    o.uv = p[vi] * vec2(0.5, -0.5) + vec2(0.5, 0.5);
    return o;
}

@group(0) @binding(0) var t: texture_2d<f32>;
@group(0) @binding(1) var s: sampler;

@fragment fn fs(in: VOut) -> Out {
    var out: Out;
    out.color = textureSample(t, s, in.uv);
    return out;
}
"#;

 
fn blit_pipeline(
    device: &wgpu::Device,
    format: wgpu::TextureFormat,
) -> Arc<wgpu::RenderPipeline> {
    static CACHE: LazyLock<Mutex<HashMap<wgpu::TextureFormat, Arc<wgpu::RenderPipeline>>>> =
        LazyLock::new(|| Mutex::new(HashMap::new()));
    let mut guard = CACHE.lock();
    let key = format;
    if let Some(p) = guard.get(&key) {
        return p.clone();
    }

    let shader = device.create_shader_module(wgpu::ShaderModuleDescriptor {
        label: Some("blit_mipmap_shader"),
        source: wgpu::ShaderSource::Wgsl(BLIT_SHADER_SRC.into()),
    });
    let bgl = device.create_bind_group_layout(&wgpu::BindGroupLayoutDescriptor {
        label: Some("blit_mipmap_bgl"),
        entries: &[
            wgpu::BindGroupLayoutEntry {
                binding: 0,
                visibility: wgpu::ShaderStages::FRAGMENT,
                ty: wgpu::BindingType::Texture {
                    sample_type: wgpu::TextureSampleType::Float { filterable: true },
                    view_dimension: wgpu::TextureViewDimension::D2,
                    multisampled: false,
                },
                count: None,
            },
            wgpu::BindGroupLayoutEntry {
                binding: 1,
                visibility: wgpu::ShaderStages::FRAGMENT,
                ty: wgpu::BindingType::Sampler(wgpu::SamplerBindingType::Filtering),
                count: None,
            },
        ],
    });
    let layout = device.create_pipeline_layout(&wgpu::PipelineLayoutDescriptor {
        label: Some("blit_mipmap_layout"),
        bind_group_layouts: &[&bgl],
        push_constant_ranges: &[],
    });
    let pipeline = Arc::new(device.create_render_pipeline(&wgpu::RenderPipelineDescriptor {
        label: Some("blit_mipmap_pipeline"),
        layout: Some(&layout),
        vertex: wgpu::VertexState {
            module: &shader,
            entry_point: "vs",
            buffers: &[],
            compilation_options: Default::default(),
        },
        fragment: Some(wgpu::FragmentState {
            module: &shader,
            entry_point: "fs",
            targets: &[Some(wgpu::ColorTargetState {
                format,
                blend: None,
                write_mask: wgpu::ColorWrites::ALL,
            })],
            compilation_options: Default::default(),
        }),
        primitive: wgpu::PrimitiveState::default(),
        depth_stencil: None,
        multisample: wgpu::MultisampleState::default(),
        multiview: None,
    }));
    guard.insert(key, pipeline.clone());
    pipeline
}

/// Generates the full mip chain of `texture` by successively downsampling the
/// previous level through a linear-filtered fullscreen blit.
fn generate_mipmaps(
    device: &wgpu::Device,
    queue: &wgpu::Queue,
    texture: &wgpu::Texture,
    mip_levels: u32,
    format: wgpu::TextureFormat,
) {
    let sampler = device.create_sampler(&wgpu::SamplerDescriptor {
        label: Some("mipmap_blit_sampler"),
        mag_filter: wgpu::FilterMode::Linear,
        min_filter: wgpu::FilterMode::Linear,
        ..Default::default()
    });
    let pipeline = blit_pipeline(device, format);
    let bgl = pipeline.get_bind_group_layout(0);

    let mut encoder = device.create_command_encoder(&wgpu::CommandEncoderDescriptor {
        label: Some("mipmap_blit_encoder"),
    });

    for level in 1..mip_levels {
        let src_view = texture.create_view(&wgpu::TextureViewDescriptor {
            label: Some("mipmap_src"),
            base_mip_level: level - 1,
            mip_level_count: Some(1),
            dimension: Some(wgpu::TextureViewDimension::D2),
            ..Default::default()
        });
        let dst_view = texture.create_view(&wgpu::TextureViewDescriptor {
            label: Some("mipmap_dst"),
            base_mip_level: level,
            mip_level_count: Some(1),
            dimension: Some(wgpu::TextureViewDimension::D2),
            ..Default::default()
        });
        let bind_group = device.create_bind_group(&wgpu::BindGroupDescriptor {
            label: Some("mipmap_blit_bg"),
            layout: &bgl,
            entries: &[
                wgpu::BindGroupEntry {
                    binding: 0,
                    resource: wgpu::BindingResource::TextureView(&src_view),
                },
                wgpu::BindGroupEntry {
                    binding: 1,
                    resource: wgpu::BindingResource::Sampler(&sampler),
                },
            ],
        });

        let mut pass = encoder.begin_render_pass(&wgpu::RenderPassDescriptor {
            label: Some("mipmap_blit_pass"),
            color_attachments: &[Some(wgpu::RenderPassColorAttachment {
                view: &dst_view,
                resolve_target: None,
                ops: wgpu::Operations {
                    load: wgpu::LoadOp::Clear(wgpu::Color::BLACK),
                    store: wgpu::StoreOp::Store,
                },
            })],
            depth_stencil_attachment: None,
            timestamp_writes: None,
            occlusion_query_set: None,
        });
        pass.set_pipeline(&pipeline);
        pass.set_bind_group(0, &bind_group, &[]);
        pass.draw(0..3, 0..1);
        drop(pass);
    }

    queue.submit(std::iter::once(encoder.finish()));
}
```

### `src/resource/toksvig.rs` | **Строк:** 152

```rust
//! Toksvig normal-map filtering for mip generation.
//!
//! When normals are averaged into a lower mip, `‖N̄‖ < 1`. Toksvig maps that
//! length loss to an additive roughness term so distant specular stays quiet:
//! `σ² = (1 − ‖N̄‖) / ‖N̄‖`.

/// Variance from the length of an averaged unit normal (Toksvig / vMF).
#[inline]
pub fn toksvig_variance(avg_normal_len: f32) -> f32 {
    let len = avg_normal_len.max(1e-4);
    ((1.0 - len) / len).max(0.0)
}

/// Convert Toksvig variance into a perceptual-roughness delta, clamped.
#[inline]
pub fn toksvig_roughness_delta(avg_normal_len: f32, max_delta: f32) -> f32 {
    let v = toksvig_variance(avg_normal_len);
    // alpha² += variance → perceptual roughly sqrt; keep a soft clamp.
    (v.sqrt() * 0.5).min(max_delta)
}

/// Decode an RGBA8 normal (tangent-space, [0,1] → [-1,1]), return unit vector.
#[inline]
pub fn decode_normal_rgba8(px: [u8; 4]) -> [f32; 3] {
    let x = (px[0] as f32 / 255.0) * 2.0 - 1.0;
    let y = (px[1] as f32 / 255.0) * 2.0 - 1.0;
    let z = (px[2] as f32 / 255.0) * 2.0 - 1.0;
    let len = (x * x + y * y + z * z).sqrt().max(1e-6);
    [x / len, y / len, z / len]
}

/// Encode a unit normal back to RGBA8; alpha stores Toksvig roughness delta
/// in [0,1] (0 = sharp, 1 = max_delta mapped).
#[inline]
pub fn encode_normal_rgba8(n: [f32; 3], roughness_delta: f32, max_delta: f32) -> [u8; 4] {
    let scale = max_delta.max(1e-6);
    [
        ((n[0] * 0.5 + 0.5) * 255.0).round().clamp(0.0, 255.0) as u8,
        ((n[1] * 0.5 + 0.5) * 255.0).round().clamp(0.0, 255.0) as u8,
        ((n[2] * 0.5 + 0.5) * 255.0).round().clamp(0.0, 255.0) as u8,
        ((roughness_delta / scale).clamp(0.0, 1.0) * 255.0).round() as u8,
    ]
}

/// Build a full Toksvig-aware mip chain from an RGBA8 normal map (mip 0).
///
/// Returns `mips[level]` as tightly packed RGBA8 bytes. Mip 0 alpha is left
/// unchanged (or 255). Higher mips store Toksvig roughness delta in alpha.
pub fn build_normal_mip_chain_toksvig(
    width: u32,
    height: u32,
    rgba: &[u8],
    max_roughness_delta: f32,
) -> Vec<Vec<u8>> {
    assert_eq!(rgba.len(), (width as usize) * (height as usize) * 4);
    let mip_levels = width.max(height).max(1).ilog2() + 1;
    let mut mips: Vec<Vec<u8>> = Vec::with_capacity(mip_levels as usize);
    mips.push(rgba.to_vec());

    let mut prev_w = width as usize;
    let mut prev_h = height as usize;

    for _level in 1..mip_levels {
        let w = (prev_w / 2).max(1);
        let h = (prev_h / 2).max(1);
        let prev = &mips[mips.len() - 1];
        let mut out = vec![0u8; w * h * 4];

        for y in 0..h {
            for x in 0..w {
                let x0 = (x * 2).min(prev_w - 1);
                let y0 = (y * 2).min(prev_h - 1);
                let x1 = (x0 + 1).min(prev_w - 1);
                let y1 = (y0 + 1).min(prev_h - 1);

                let samples = [
                    read_px(prev, prev_w, x0, y0),
                    read_px(prev, prev_w, x1, y0),
                    read_px(prev, prev_w, x0, y1),
                    read_px(prev, prev_w, x1, y1),
                ];

                let mut sx = 0.0f32;
                let mut sy = 0.0f32;
                let mut sz = 0.0f32;
                for s in samples {
                    let n = decode_normal_rgba8(s);
                    sx += n[0];
                    sy += n[1];
                    sz += n[2];
                }
                sx *= 0.25;
                sy *= 0.25;
                sz *= 0.25;
                let avg_len = (sx * sx + sy * sy + sz * sz).sqrt();
                let inv = if avg_len > 1e-6 { 1.0 / avg_len } else { 1.0 };
                let n = [sx * inv, sy * inv, sz * inv];
                let delta = toksvig_roughness_delta(avg_len, max_roughness_delta);
                let enc = encode_normal_rgba8(n, delta, max_roughness_delta);
                let i = (y * w + x) * 4;
                out[i..i + 4].copy_from_slice(&enc);
            }
        }

        mips.push(out);
        prev_w = w;
        prev_h = h;
    }

    mips
}

#[inline]
fn read_px(buf: &[u8], width: usize, x: usize, y: usize) -> [u8; 4] {
    let i = (y * width + x) * 4;
    [buf[i], buf[i + 1], buf[i + 2], buf[i + 3]]
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn unit_normal_has_zero_variance() {
        assert!(toksvig_variance(1.0) < 1e-5);
    }

    #[test]
    fn short_normal_raises_roughness() {
        let d = toksvig_roughness_delta(0.5, 0.5);
        assert!(d > 0.1);
    }

    #[test]
    fn mip_chain_shrinks() {
        let w = 4u32;
        let h = 4u32;
        let mut rgba = vec![0u8; (w * h * 4) as usize];
        // Flat +Z normals
        for px in rgba.chunks_exact_mut(4) {
            px[0] = 128;
            px[1] = 128;
            px[2] = 255;
            px[3] = 255;
        }
        let mips = build_normal_mip_chain_toksvig(w, h, &rgba, 0.5);
        assert_eq!(mips.len(), 3); // 4→2→1
        assert_eq!(mips[1].len(), 2 * 2 * 4);
        assert_eq!(mips[2].len(), 1 * 1 * 4);
    }
}
```

```rust
//! Sparse brick-atlas registry (CPU side).
//!
//! [`SdfBrickAtlas`] maps mesh ids to baked 64³ distance-field bricks. It is
//! the **CPU-side registry**. GPU upload lives in [`crate::sdf::gpu_atlas`]:
//! up to 8 bricks are packed into a 128³ atlas with a page table consumed by
//! `pbr.wgsl` / `sdf_shadow.wgsl`.
//!
//! GPU-upload notes for the future task:
//! * Pack each brick's `DistanceField64::data` into a single-channel format
//!   (`r16snorm` halves memory vs `r32float` with no practical precision
//!   loss for shadow tracing; keep `r32float` as the debug path).
//! * A brick occupies a contiguous 64³ sub-region ("page") of the atlas;
//!   [`BrickRef::index`] already provides a stable slot number to hang a
//!   page coordinate off.
//! * The WGSL companion (`shaders/sdf_shadow.wgsl`) and `pbr.wgsl` sample the
//!   GPU atlas via the multi-brick page table in [`crate::sdf::SdfSceneGpu`].

use super::bake::DistanceField64;
use redox_math::Vec3;
use std::collections::HashMap;

/// One placed distance-field brick.
#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
pub struct SdfBrick {
    /// Baked signed distance field (64³ texels).
    pub field: DistanceField64,
    /// World-space centre of the brick's domain cube.
    pub origin_ws: Vec3,
    /// Side length of the brick's domain cube in meters.
    pub world_size: Vec3,
}

impl SdfBrick {
    /// Half-extent of the domain cube.
    #[inline]
    pub fn half_size(&self) -> Vec3 {
        self.world_size * 0.5
    }

    /// True when `p` (world space) lies inside the brick's domain.
    #[inline]
    pub fn contains(&self, p: Vec3) -> bool {
        let d = (p - self.origin_ws).abs();
        d.x <= self.half_size().x && d.y <= self.half_size().y && d.z <= self.half_size().z
    }

    /// Trilinear signed-distance sample at world-space `p`. Only meaningful
    /// when [`Self::contains`] holds; outside positions clamp to the border
    /// texels.
    #[inline]
    pub fn sample_world(&self, p: Vec3) -> f32 {
        self.field.sample(p - self.origin_ws)
    }
}

/// Stable handle from a mesh id to its brick slot in [`SdfBrickAtlas`].
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct BrickRef {
    /// Index into [`SdfBrickAtlas::bricks`].
    pub index: u32,
}

/// Registry of baked SDF bricks keyed by mesh id.
///
/// Re-inserting an existing id replaces that brick **in place**, keeping
/// every other [`BrickRef`] valid — important once refs are handed out to
/// render objects.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, Default)]
pub struct SdfBrickAtlas {
    entries: HashMap<u64, BrickRef>,
    bricks: Vec<SdfBrick>,
}

impl SdfBrickAtlas {
    pub fn new() -> Self {
        Self::default()
    }

    /// Inserts (or replaces) the brick for `id`.
    pub fn insert(&mut self, id: u64, brick: SdfBrick) {
        match self.entries.get(&id) {
            Some(&BrickRef { index }) => self.bricks[index as usize] = brick,
            None => {
                let index = self.bricks.len() as u32;
                self.bricks.push(brick);
                self.entries.insert(id, BrickRef { index });
            }
        }
    }

    /// Returns the brick registered for `id`, if any.
    pub fn get(&self, id: u64) -> Option<&SdfBrick> {
        self.entries
            .get(&id)
            .map(|r| &self.bricks[r.index as usize])
    }

    /// Number of bricks in the registry.
    #[inline]
    pub fn len(&self) -> usize {
        self.bricks.len()
    }

    #[inline]
    pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool {
        self.bricks.is_empty()
    }

    /// Iterates all placed bricks (slot order).
    pub fn iter(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = &SdfBrick> {
        self.bricks.iter()
    }

    /// Total CPU memory occupied by field data, in bytes (metadata excluded).
    pub fn total_bytes(&self) -> usize {
        self.bricks.iter().map(|b| b.field.data.len() * 4).sum()
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use crate::mesh::primitive::create_cube;

    #[test]
    fn atlas_insert_get_roundtrip() {
        // Bake a real field so byte accounting reflects production use.
        let cube = create_cube();
        let field = crate::sdf::bake_mesh(&cube, Vec3::splat(2.0));

        let mut atlas = SdfBrickAtlas::new();
        assert!(atlas.is_empty());
        assert_eq!(atlas.total_bytes(), 0);
        assert!(atlas.get(42).is_none());

        atlas.insert(
            42,
            SdfBrick {
                field: field.clone(),
                origin_ws: Vec3::new(10.0, 0.0, -5.0),
                world_size: Vec3::splat(2.0),
            },
        );
        assert_eq!(atlas.len(), 1);
        assert_eq!(atlas.total_bytes(), 64 * 64 * 64 * 4);

        let brick = atlas.get(42).expect("brick must round-trip");
        assert_eq!(brick.origin_ws, Vec3::new(10.0, 0.0, -5.0));
        assert_eq!(brick.world_size, Vec3::splat(2.0));
        assert_eq!(brick.field.data[0], field.data[0]);
        assert!(brick.contains(Vec3::new(10.0, 0.9, -5.0)));
        assert!(!brick.contains(Vec3::new(13.0, 0.0, -5.0)));

        // Re-inserting replaces in place instead of appending a slot.
        atlas.insert(
            42,
            SdfBrick {
                field,
                origin_ws: Vec3::ZERO,
                world_size: Vec3::splat(4.0),
            },
        );
        assert_eq!(atlas.len(), 1);
        assert_eq!(atlas.get(42).unwrap().origin_ws, Vec3::ZERO);

        // Distinct ids get distinct slots.
        atlas.insert(
            7,
            SdfBrick {
                field: DistanceField64 {
                    data: vec![1.0; 64 * 64 * 64],
                    world_size: Vec3::ONE,
                },
                origin_ws: Vec3::ZERO,
                world_size: Vec3::ONE,
            },
        );
        assert_eq!(atlas.len(), 2);
        assert_eq!(atlas.total_bytes(), 2 * 64 * 64 * 64 * 4);
    }
}
```

### `src/sdf/bake.rs` | **Строк:** 523

```rust
//! CPU baking of 64³ signed distance fields from triangle meshes.
//!
//! # Algorithm
//!
//! 1. All triangles are extracted into a flat array and wrapped in a
//!    median-split Bounding Volume Hierarchy (longest-axis split, leaf
//!    capacity 4, flat node pool).
//! 2. The field domain is the axis-aligned cube of side `world_size`
//!    centred on the mesh AABB centre. Texel `(x, y, z)` stores the signed
//!    distance at the texel centre
//!    `centre + world_size * ((x,y,z) + 0.5) / 64 - world_size / 2`,
//!    i.e. texel centres sit at half-texel offsets from the domain faces.
//! 3. Unsigned distance: exact closest-point-on-mesh query through the BVH
//!    (best-first branch-and-bound over node AABBs, Ericson's
//!    point-in-closest-triangle test per visited leaf).
//! 4. Sign: negative inside the solid, positive outside (the standard SDF
//!    convention), stored in meters.
//!
//! ## Sign method — ray parity (chosen deliberately)
//!
//! The plan allowed either ray parity or the triangle-winding heuristic
//! (`dot(triangle_normal, texel - closest_point)`). We use **ray parity**:
//! a ray is cast from the texel centre in a fixed, non-axis-aligned
//! direction and mesh intersections are counted via the BVH; an odd count
//! means the point is inside. The winding heuristic was rejected because it
//! systematically mis-signs points whose nearest surface feature is an edge
//! or vertex shared by faces with different normals — every convex corner
//! of a cube, for example, where the closest triangle's face normal points
//! sideways while the texel sits outside along the diagonal. Parity only
//! assumes a watertight, consistently wound mesh, which is the same
//! assumption every downstream consumer (shadows, DDGI) makes. Points
//! outside the mesh AABB skip the ray cast entirely (they are provably
//! outside the solid).
//!
//! Baked fields are pure CPU data; packing them into the GPU 128³ brick
//! atlas happens in a later phase (see [`crate::sdf::atlas`]).

use crate::mesh::Mesh;
use redox_math::Vec3;

/// Field resolution along each axis (64³ texels per brick).
pub const SDF_RESOLUTION: usize = 64;

/// A baked 64³ signed distance field covering a cubic world-space domain.
///
/// The domain is centred on the baked mesh's AABB centre; callers that need
/// absolute world placement wrap the field in an
/// [`crate::sdf::SdfBrick`], which carries `origin_ws` (the world-space
/// centre of the domain) alongside the field.
#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
pub struct DistanceField64 {
    /// Signed distance in meters at each texel centre.
    ///
    /// Indexing: `i = (z * SDF_RESOLUTION + y) * SDF_RESOLUTION + x`
    /// (x fastest). Negative = inside the solid.
    pub data: Vec<f32>,
    /// Side length of the cubic (recommended) domain in meters.
    pub world_size: Vec3,
}

impl DistanceField64 {
    /// Linear index into [`Self::data`] for texel `(x, y, z)`.
    #[inline]
    pub fn index(x: usize, y: usize, z: usize) -> usize {
        (z * SDF_RESOLUTION + y) * SDF_RESOLUTION + x
    }

    /// Size of one texel edge in meters per axis.
    #[inline]
    pub fn texel_world_size(&self) -> Vec3 {
        self.world_size / SDF_RESOLUTION as f32
    }

    /// Trilinearly samples the field at domain-local coordinates
    /// (`p` relative to the domain centre, in meters; the domain spans
    /// `±world_size / 2`). Positions outside the domain clamp to the
    /// border texels.
    pub fn sample(&self, local: Vec3) -> f32 {
        // Continuous grid coordinate in [-0.5 * (RES-1), 0.5 * (RES-1)].
        let g = (local / self.world_size + Vec3::splat(0.5)) * Vec3::splat(SDF_RESOLUTION as f32)
            - Vec3::splat(0.5);
        let lo = g.floor();
        let fr = g - lo;
        let clampi =
            |v: f32| -> usize { v.round().clamp(0.0, (SDF_RESOLUTION - 1) as f32) as usize };
        let x0 = clampi(lo.x);
        let y0 = clampi(lo.y);
        let z0 = clampi(lo.z);
        let x1 = (x0 + 1).min(SDF_RESOLUTION - 1);
        let y1 = (y0 + 1).min(SDF_RESOLUTION - 1);
        let z1 = (z0 + 1).min(SDF_RESOLUTION - 1);
        let (fx, fy, fz) = (fr.x, fr.y, fr.z);
        let d = &self.data;
        let c00 = d[Self::index(x0, y0, z0)].mul_add(1.0 - fx, d[Self::index(x1, y0, z0)] * fx);
        let c10 = d[Self::index(x0, y1, z0)].mul_add(1.0 - fx, d[Self::index(x1, y1, z0)] * fx);
        let c01 = d[Self::index(x0, y0, z1)].mul_add(1.0 - fx, d[Self::index(x1, y0, z1)] * fx);
        let c11 = d[Self::index(x0, y1, z1)].mul_add(1.0 - fx, d[Self::index(x1, y1, z1)] * fx);
        let c0 = c00.mul_add(1.0 - fy, c10 * fy);
        let c1 = c01.mul_add(1.0 - fy, c11 * fy);
        c0.mul_add(1.0 - fz, c1 * fz)
    }
}

/// Bakes a 64³ signed distance field for `mesh` over a domain of side
/// `world_size` centred on the mesh AABB centre. An empty mesh yields a
/// uniformly "far outside" field.
pub fn bake_mesh(mesh: &Mesh, world_size: Vec3) -> DistanceField64 {
    let tri_count = mesh.indices.len() / 3;
    debug_assert_eq!(
        mesh.indices.len() % 3,
        0,
        "mesh index buffer must be a multiple of 3"
    );

    if tri_count == 0 {
        return DistanceField64 {
            data: vec![world_size.max_element(); SDF_RESOLUTION.pow(3)],
            world_size,
        };
    }

    let mut tris = Vec::with_capacity(tri_count);
    for tri in mesh.indices.chunks_exact(3) {
        let a = mesh.vertices[tri[0] as usize].position;
        let b = mesh.vertices[tri[1] as usize].position;
        let c = mesh.vertices[tri[2] as usize].position;
        tris.push([
            Vec3::new(a[0], a[1], a[2]),
            Vec3::new(b[0], b[1], b[2]),
            Vec3::new(c[0], c[1], c[2]),
        ]);
    }
    let bvh = TriBvh::new(tris);

    let centre = mesh.aabb.center();
    let res = SDF_RESOLUTION as f32;
    // Points provably outside the (slightly inflated) mesh AABB are outside
    // the solid — skips the parity ray cast for most exterior texels.
    let eps = 1.0e-4;
    let outer_min = mesh.aabb.min - Vec3::splat(eps);
    let outer_max = mesh.aabb.max + Vec3::splat(eps);

    let mut data = vec![0.0f32; SDF_RESOLUTION.pow(3)];
    for z in 0..SDF_RESOLUTION {
        let lz = ((z as f32 + 0.5) / res - 0.5) * world_size.z;
        for y in 0..SDF_RESOLUTION {
            let ly = ((y as f32 + 0.5) / res - 0.5) * world_size.y;
            for x in 0..SDF_RESOLUTION {
                let lx = ((x as f32 + 0.5) / res - 0.5) * world_size.x;
                let local = Vec3::new(lx, ly, lz);
                let p = centre + local;
                let dist = bvh.closest_distance(p);
                let inside = p.x > outer_min.x
                    && p.y > outer_min.y
                    && p.z > outer_min.z
                    && p.x < outer_max.x
                    && p.y < outer_max.y
                    && p.z < outer_max.z;
                let sign = if inside && bvh.parity_inside(p) {
                    -1.0
                } else {
                    1.0
                };
                data[DistanceField64::index(x, y, z)] = sign * dist;
            }
        }
    }

    DistanceField64 { data, world_size }
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Triangle BVH
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

const MAX_LEAF_TRIS: usize = 4;
/// Fixed parity ray direction.
///
/// Two requirements. (1) Not axis-aligned, so it never runs parallel to the
/// dominant face planes of typical axis-aligned meshes. (2) The component
/// **ratios must be irrational** — with a rational direction such as
/// `normalize(2, 3, 5)`, rays cast from dyadic-grid texel centres hit mesh
/// edges *exactly* in f32 arithmetic in systematic line families (the
/// preimage planes of each edge intersect the texel lattice in lattice
/// lines), double-counting crossings and flipping the parity sign for those
/// texels. Irrational ratios (φ and √3 here) make exact edge hits
/// measure-zero accidents instead of a systematic failure mode.
const PARITY_DIR: Vec3 = Vec3::new(0.388_738_4, 0.628_942_5, 0.673_264_2); // normalize(1, φ, √3)

struct BvhNode {
    bmin: Vec3,
    bmax: Vec3,
    /// Leaf: index of the first triangle in `tri_order`.
    /// Internal: index of the left child (right child is `left_first + 1`).
    left_first: u32,
    /// Leaf: number of triangles. Internal: 0.
    count: u32,
}

/// Flat median-split BVH over triangles, supporting exact closest-point
/// queries and ray-intersection counting (for the parity sign test).
struct TriBvh {
    nodes: Vec<BvhNode>,
    /// Triangle indices in BVH leaf order.
    tri_order: Vec<u32>,
    /// Flat triangle storage: 3 vertices per triangle.
    tris: Vec<[Vec3; 3]>,
}

impl TriBvh {
    fn new(tris: Vec<[Vec3; 3]>) -> Self {
        let tri_count = tris.len();
        let centroids: Vec<Vec3> = tris.iter().map(|t| (t[0] + t[1] + t[2]) / 3.0).collect();
        let mut bvh = Self {
            nodes: Vec::with_capacity(2 * tri_count),
            tri_order: (0..tri_count as u32).collect(),
            tris,
        };
        if tri_count > 0 {
            bvh.nodes.push(BvhNode {
                bmin: Vec3::ZERO,
                bmax: Vec3::ZERO,
                left_first: 0,
                count: 0,
            });
            bvh.build_into(0, 0, tri_count as u32, &centroids);
        }
        bvh
    }

    /// Recursively fills `slot` with the node covering triangle range
    /// `[start, end)` (indices into `tri_order`).
    ///
    /// The two children of an internal node are allocated **adjacently**
    /// (left at `left_first`, right at `left_first + 1`) before either is
    /// filled, which is the layout the traversal routines rely on.
    fn build_into(&mut self, slot: u32, start: u32, end: u32, centroids: &[Vec3]) {
        let (bmin, bmax) = self.range_bounds(start, end);
        let count = (end - start) as usize;
        self.nodes[slot as usize] = BvhNode {
            bmin,
            bmax,
            left_first: start,
            count: end - start,
        };

        if count <= MAX_LEAF_TRIS {
            return;
        }

        // Median split on the longest axis of the node bounds.
        let extents = bmax - bmin;
        let axis = if extents.x >= extents.y && extents.x >= extents.z {
            0
        } else if extents.y >= extents.z {
            1
        } else {
            2
        };
        let get_c = |t: u32| -> f32 {
            let c = centroids[t as usize];
            [c.x, c.y, c.z][axis]
        };
        self.tri_order[start as usize..end as usize]
            .sort_by(|&a, &b| get_c(a).partial_cmp(&get_c(b)).unwrap());
        let mid = start + (count / 2) as u32;

        let left_idx = self.nodes.len() as u32;
        for _ in 0..2 {
            self.nodes.push(BvhNode {
                bmin: Vec3::ZERO,
                bmax: Vec3::ZERO,
                left_first: 0,
                count: 0,
            });
        }
        self.build_into(left_idx, start, mid, centroids);
        self.build_into(left_idx + 1, mid, end, centroids);
        let node = &mut self.nodes[slot as usize];
        node.left_first = left_idx;
        node.count = 0;
    }

    fn range_bounds(&self, start: u32, end: u32) -> (Vec3, Vec3) {
        let mut bmin = Vec3::splat(f32::INFINITY);
        let mut bmax = Vec3::splat(f32::NEG_INFINITY);
        for &t in &self.tri_order[start as usize..end as usize] {
            for v in &self.tris[t as usize] {
                bmin = bmin.min(*v);
                bmax = bmax.max(*v);
            }
        }
        (bmin, bmax)
    }

    /// Squared distance from `p` to an AABB (0 inside).
    #[inline]
    fn aabb_dist_sq(p: Vec3, bmin: Vec3, bmax: Vec3) -> f32 {
        let dx = (bmin.x - p.x).max(p.x - bmax.x).max(0.0);
        let dy = (bmin.y - p.y).max(p.y - bmax.y).max(0.0);
        let dz = (bmin.z - p.z).max(p.z - bmax.z).max(0.0);
        dx * dx + dy * dy + dz * dz
    }

    /// Exact distance from `p` to the closest point on any triangle,
    /// via best-first branch-and-bound traversal.
    fn closest_distance(&self, p: Vec3) -> f32 {
        use std::cmp::Reverse;
        use std::collections::BinaryHeap;

        if self.nodes.is_empty() {
            return f32::INFINITY;
        }
        // Positive f32 bit patterns order identically to the values, so the
        // bit pattern doubles as a comparable heap key.
        let mut best = f32::INFINITY;
        let mut heap: BinaryHeap<(Reverse<u32>, u32)> = BinaryHeap::new();
        let root_bound = Self::aabb_dist_sq(p, self.nodes[0].bmin, self.nodes[0].bmax);
        heap.push((Reverse(root_bound.to_bits()), 0));

        while let Some((Reverse(bound_bits), ni)) = heap.pop() {
            // Every remaining node is at least this far away — done.
            if f32::from_bits(bound_bits) >= best {
                break;
            }
            let node = &self.nodes[ni as usize];
            if node.count > 0 {
                for &t in &self.tri_order
                    [node.left_first as usize..(node.left_first + node.count) as usize]
                {
                    let tri = &self.tris[t as usize];
                    let cp = closest_point_on_triangle(p, tri[0], tri[1], tri[2]);
                    let d2 = (cp - p).length_squared();
                    if d2 < best {
                        best = d2;
                    }
                }
            } else {
                for child in [node.left_first, node.left_first + 1] {
                    let c = &self.nodes[child as usize];
                    let b = Self::aabb_dist_sq(p, c.bmin, c.bmax);
                    if b < best {
                        heap.push((Reverse(b.to_bits()), child));
                    }
                }
            }
        }
        best.sqrt()
    }

    /// Counts ray-triangle intersections along the fixed parity direction.
    fn count_ray_hits(&self, origin: Vec3) -> u32 {
        let d = PARITY_DIR;
        let inv = Vec3::new(1.0 / d.x, 1.0 / d.y, 1.0 / d.z);
        let mut hits = 0u32;
        let mut stack = vec![0u32];
        while let Some(ni) = stack.pop() {
            let node = &self.nodes[ni as usize];
            if !ray_intersects_aabb(origin, inv, node.bmin, node.bmax) {
                continue;
            }
            if node.count > 0 {
                for &t in &self.tri_order
                    [node.left_first as usize..(node.left_first + node.count) as usize]
                {
                    let tri = &self.tris[t as usize];
                    if ray_triangle_t(origin, d, tri[0], tri[1], tri[2]).is_some() {
                        hits += 1;
                    }
                }
            } else {
                stack.push(node.left_first);
                stack.push(node.left_first + 1);
            }
        }
        hits
    }

    /// True when `p` is inside the closed mesh surface (odd ray parity).
    fn parity_inside(&self, p: Vec3) -> bool {
        self.count_ray_hits(p) % 2 == 1
    }
}

/// Ericson, *Real-Time Collision Detection* §5.1.6: closest point on a
/// triangle to `p`.
fn closest_point_on_triangle(p: Vec3, a: Vec3, b: Vec3, c: Vec3) -> Vec3 {
    let ab = b - a;
    let ac = c - a;
    let ap = p - a;
    let d1 = ab.dot(ap);
    let d2 = ac.dot(ap);
    if d1 <= 0.0 && d2 <= 0.0 {
        return a;
    }
    let bp = p - b;
    let d3 = ab.dot(bp);
    let d4 = ac.dot(bp);
    if d3 >= 0.0 && d4 <= d3 {
        return b;
    }
    let vc = d1 * d4 - d3 * d2;
    if vc <= 0.0 && d1 >= 0.0 && d3 <= 0.0 {
        let v = d1 / (d1 - d3);
        return a + ab * v;
    }
    let cp = p - c;
    let d5 = ab.dot(cp);
    let d6 = ac.dot(cp);
    if d6 >= 0.0 && d5 <= d6 {
        return c;
    }
    let vb = d5 * d2 - d1 * d6;
    if vb <= 0.0 && d2 >= 0.0 && d6 <= 0.0 {
        let w = d2 / (d2 - d6);
        return a + ac * w;
    }
    let va = d3 * d6 - d5 * d4;
    if va <= 0.0 && (d4 - d3) >= 0.0 && (d5 - d6) >= 0.0 {
        let w = (d4 - d3) / ((d4 - d3) + (d5 - d6));
        return b + (c - b) * w;
    }
    let denom = 1.0 / (va + vb + vc);
    let v = vb * denom;
    let w = vc * denom;
    a + ab * v + ac * w
}

/// Slab test between the ray `(origin, inv_dir)` and an AABB. `inv_dir` may
/// contain infinities for zero direction components (never NaN here because
/// the parity direction is component-wise non-zero).
fn ray_intersects_aabb(origin: Vec3, inv_dir: Vec3, bmin: Vec3, bmax: Vec3) -> bool {
    let mut tmin = 0.0f32;
    let mut tmax = f32::INFINITY;
    let o = [origin.x, origin.y, origin.z];
    let inv = [inv_dir.x, inv_dir.y, inv_dir.z];
    let mn = [bmin.x, bmin.y, bmin.z];
    let mx = [bmax.x, bmax.y, bmax.z];
    for a in 0..3 {
        let t1 = (mn[a] - o[a]) * inv[a];
        let t2 = (mx[a] - o[a]) * inv[a];
        tmin = tmin.max(t1.min(t2));
        tmax = tmax.min(t1.max(t2));
    }
    tmax >= tmin
}

/// Möller–Trumbore ray-triangle intersection; returns the ray parameter
/// `t > 1e-5` on hit.
fn ray_triangle_t(o: Vec3, d: Vec3, a: Vec3, b: Vec3, c: Vec3) -> Option<f32> {
    let e1 = b - a;
    let e2 = c - a;
    let h = d.cross(e2);
    let det = e1.dot(h);
    if det.abs() < 1.0e-12 {
        return None;
    }
    let f = 1.0 / det;
    let s = o - a;
    let u = f * s.dot(h);
    if !(0.0..=1.0).contains(&u) {
        return None;
    }
    let q = s.cross(e1);
    let v = f * d.dot(q);
    if v < 0.0 || u + v > 1.0 {
        return None;
    }
    let t = f * e2.dot(q);
    (t > 1.0e-5).then_some(t)
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use crate::mesh::primitive::create_cube;

    #[test]
    fn baked_cube_signs_and_distances() {
        let cube = create_cube();
        let field = bake_mesh(&cube, Vec3::splat(2.0));
        assert_eq!(field.data.len(), 64 * 64 * 64);
        assert_eq!(field.world_size, Vec3::splat(2.0));

        // Texel centres sit at ±0.015625 m around the origin for this
        // domain, so none lands exactly on the surface (±0.5 m).
        // Domain-centre texel: 0.484375 m from every face → negative.
        let c = field.data[DistanceField64::index(32, 32, 32)];
        assert!(
            (c + 0.484_375).abs() < 1.0e-3,
            "interior centre texel should be ~-0.484375, got {c}"
        );

        // Half a texel beyond the +X face: exactly one texel edge out.
        let e = field.data[DistanceField64::index(63, 32, 32)];
        assert!(
            (e - 0.484_375).abs() < 1.0e-3,
            "exterior face texel should be ~+0.484375, got {e}"
        );

        // Outside along the diagonal: sqrt(3) times the axis distance.
        let k = field.data[DistanceField64::index(63, 63, 63)];
        let expected = 0.484_375f32 * 3.0f32.sqrt();
        assert!(
            (k - expected).abs() < 2.0e-3,
            "corner exterior texel should be ~{expected}, got {k}"
        );

        // Ray parity must classify exactly the 32³ interior texels as
        // negative — a strict whole-field invariant for the unit cube.
        let negatives = field.data.iter().filter(|&&d| d < 0.0).count();
        assert_eq!(negatives, 32 * 32 * 32, "wrong interior texel count");

        // The nearest texel centres sit one texel edge (0.015625 m) off
        // the faces — no zero crossings, no missed surface.
        let min_abs = field.data.iter().fold(f32::MAX, |a, &d| a.min(d.abs()));
        assert!(
            min_abs > 0.01 && min_abs < 0.03,
            "minimum |distance| should be about one texel, got {min_abs}"
        );
    }
}
```

```rust
//! GPU 128³ SDF brick atlas with a multi-brick page table for PBR sampling.
//!
//! The atlas packs up to [`MAX_SDF_BRICKS`] 64³ bricks into a 2×2×2 page grid
//! inside the 128³ volume. [`SdfSceneGpu`] carries the page table so
//! `pbr.wgsl` / `sdf_shadow.wgsl` can sample more than one brick.

use bytemuck::{Pod, Zeroable};

use super::bake::SDF_RESOLUTION;
use super::SdfBrick;

/// Side length of the global 3D atlas texture (texels per axis).
pub const GPU_ATLAS_EXTENT: u32 = 128;

/// Maximum bricks packed into the 128³ atlas (2×2×2 pages of 64³).
pub const MAX_SDF_BRICKS: usize = 8;

/// One page-table entry: world AABB + atlas texel origin.
/// Mirrored in `pbr.wgsl` / `sdf_shadow.wgsl` as `SdfBrickPageGpu`.
#[repr(C)]
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Pod, Zeroable)]
pub struct SdfBrickPageGpu {
    /// World-space AABB min (xyz); w unused.
    pub world_min: [f32; 4],
    /// World-space AABB max (xyz); w unused.
    pub world_max: [f32; 4],
    /// Atlas texel origin (xyz) + brick resolution in texels (w, typically 64).
    pub atlas_origin_res: [f32; 4],
}

impl Default for SdfBrickPageGpu {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self {
            world_min: [0.0; 4],
            world_max: [0.0; 4],
            atlas_origin_res: [0.0, 0.0, 0.0, SDF_RESOLUTION as f32],
        }
    }
}

/// Scene descriptor mirrored in `pbr.wgsl` / `sdf_shadow.wgsl` (`@binding(26)`).
///
/// Layout (16-byte aligned):
/// * `atlas_dims` — x = brick count, yzw reserved / brick resolution in w
/// * `world_bounds_min` / `world_bounds_max_texel` — union AABB + texel size in w
/// * `pages` — up to [`MAX_SDF_BRICKS`] page-table entries
#[repr(C)]
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Pod, Zeroable)]
pub struct SdfSceneGpu {
    pub atlas_dims: [u32; 4],
    pub world_bounds_min: [f32; 4],
    pub world_bounds_max_texel: [f32; 4],
    pub pages: [SdfBrickPageGpu; MAX_SDF_BRICKS],
}

/// Single-channel 128³ distance-field atlas on the GPU.
pub struct SdfGpuAtlas {
    pub texture: wgpu::Texture,
    pub view: wgpu::TextureView,
    pub sampler: wgpu::Sampler,
    pub scene_buffer: wgpu::Buffer,
    pub scene: SdfSceneGpu,
    pub enabled: bool,
}

impl SdfGpuAtlas {
    /// Creates an empty atlas (large positive distances) with a default scene uniform.
    pub fn new(device: &wgpu::Device, queue: &wgpu::Queue) -> Self {
        let extent = GPU_ATLAS_EXTENT;
        let texture = device.create_texture(&wgpu::TextureDescriptor {
            label: Some("sdf_brick_atlas_128"),
            size: wgpu::Extent3d {
                width: extent,
                height: extent,
                depth_or_array_layers: extent,
            },
            mip_level_count: 1,
            sample_count: 1,
            dimension: wgpu::TextureDimension::D3,
            format: wgpu::TextureFormat::R32Float,
            usage: wgpu::TextureUsages::TEXTURE_BINDING | wgpu::TextureUsages::COPY_DST,
            view_formats: &[],
        });
        let view = texture.create_view(&wgpu::TextureViewDescriptor {
            label: Some("sdf_brick_atlas_view"),
            dimension: Some(wgpu::TextureViewDimension::D3),
            ..Default::default()
        });
        let sampler = device.create_sampler(&wgpu::SamplerDescriptor {
            label: Some("sdf_brick_sampler"),
            address_mode_u: wgpu::AddressMode::ClampToEdge,
            address_mode_v: wgpu::AddressMode::ClampToEdge,
            address_mode_w: wgpu::AddressMode::ClampToEdge,
            mag_filter: wgpu::FilterMode::Nearest,
            min_filter: wgpu::FilterMode::Nearest,
            ..Default::default()
        });

        let far = 1.0e6_f32;
        let voxels = (extent * extent * extent) as usize;
        let init_data = vec![far; voxels];
        queue.write_texture(
            wgpu::ImageCopyTexture {
                texture: &texture,
                mip_level: 0,
                origin: wgpu::Origin3d::ZERO,
                aspect: wgpu::TextureAspect::All,
            },
            bytemuck::cast_slice(&init_data),
            wgpu::ImageDataLayout {
                offset: 0,
                bytes_per_row: Some(extent * 4),
                rows_per_image: Some(extent),
            },
            wgpu::Extent3d {
                width: extent,
                height: extent,
                depth_or_array_layers: extent,
            },
        );

        let scene = SdfSceneGpu {
            atlas_dims: [0, 0, 0, SDF_RESOLUTION as u32],
            world_bounds_min: [0.0; 4],
            world_bounds_max_texel: [1.0, 1.0, 1.0, 0.01],
            pages: [SdfBrickPageGpu::default(); MAX_SDF_BRICKS],
        };
        let scene_buffer = device.create_buffer(&wgpu::BufferDescriptor {
            label: Some("sdf_scene_uniform"),
            size: std::mem::size_of::<SdfSceneGpu>() as u64,
            usage: wgpu::BufferUsages::UNIFORM | wgpu::BufferUsages::COPY_DST,
            mapped_at_creation: false,
        });
        queue.write_buffer(&scene_buffer, 0, bytemuck::bytes_of(&scene));

        Self {
            texture,
            view,
            sampler,
            scene_buffer,
            scene,
            enabled: false,
        }
    }

    /// Packs one brick into page slot 0 (compat helper).
    pub fn upload_brick(&mut self, queue: &wgpu::Queue, brick: &SdfBrick) {
        self.upload_bricks(queue, std::slice::from_ref(brick));
    }

    /// Packs up to [`MAX_SDF_BRICKS`] bricks into the 2×2×2 page grid and uploads
    /// the page table + atlas voxels.
    pub fn upload_bricks(&mut self, queue: &wgpu::Queue, bricks: &[SdfBrick]) {
        let count = bricks.len().min(MAX_SDF_BRICKS);
        if count == 0 {
            self.scene.atlas_dims[0] = 0;
            queue.write_buffer(&self.scene_buffer, 0, bytemuck::bytes_of(&self.scene));
            self.enabled = false;
            return;
        }

        let res = SDF_RESOLUTION as u32;
        let pages_per_axis = 2u32; // 128 / 64
        let mut pages = [SdfBrickPageGpu::default(); MAX_SDF_BRICKS];
        let mut bounds_min = bricks[0].origin_ws - bricks[0].half_size();
        let mut bounds_max = bricks[0].origin_ws + bricks[0].half_size();
        let mut min_texel = bricks[0].field.texel_world_size().x;

        // Clear atlas to "far outside".
        let mut voxels =
            vec![1.0e6_f32; (GPU_ATLAS_EXTENT * GPU_ATLAS_EXTENT * GPU_ATLAS_EXTENT) as usize];

        for (i, brick) in bricks.iter().take(count).enumerate() {
            let px = (i as u32) % pages_per_axis;
            let py = ((i as u32) / pages_per_axis) % pages_per_axis;
            let pz = (i as u32) / (pages_per_axis * pages_per_axis);
            let origin_x = px * res;
            let origin_y = py * res;
            let origin_z = pz * res;

            let half = brick.half_size();
            let bmin = brick.origin_ws - half;
            let bmax = brick.origin_ws + half;
            bounds_min = bounds_min.min(bmin);
            bounds_max = bounds_max.max(bmax);
            min_texel = min_texel.min(brick.field.texel_world_size().x);

            pages[i] = SdfBrickPageGpu {
                world_min: [bmin.x, bmin.y, bmin.z, 0.0],
                world_max: [bmax.x, bmax.y, bmax.z, 0.0],
                atlas_origin_res: [
                    origin_x as f32,
                    origin_y as f32,
                    origin_z as f32,
                    res as f32,
                ],
            };

            for z in 0..SDF_RESOLUTION {
                for y in 0..SDF_RESOLUTION {
                    for x in 0..SDF_RESOLUTION {
                        let src = super::bake::DistanceField64::index(x, y, z);
                        let dst_x = origin_x as usize + x;
                        let dst_y = origin_y as usize + y;
                        let dst_z = origin_z as usize + z;
                        let dst = (dst_z * GPU_ATLAS_EXTENT as usize + dst_y)
                            * GPU_ATLAS_EXTENT as usize
                            + dst_x;
                        voxels[dst] = brick.field.data[src];
                    }
                }
            }
        }

        self.scene = SdfSceneGpu {
            atlas_dims: [
                count as u32,
                pages_per_axis,
                pages_per_axis,
                SDF_RESOLUTION as u32,
            ],
            world_bounds_min: [bounds_min.x, bounds_min.y, bounds_min.z, 0.0],
            world_bounds_max_texel: [bounds_max.x, bounds_max.y, bounds_max.z, min_texel],
            pages,
        };
        queue.write_buffer(&self.scene_buffer, 0, bytemuck::bytes_of(&self.scene));

        queue.write_texture(
            wgpu::ImageCopyTexture {
                texture: &self.texture,
                mip_level: 0,
                origin: wgpu::Origin3d::ZERO,
                aspect: wgpu::TextureAspect::All,
            },
            bytemuck::cast_slice(&voxels),
            wgpu::ImageDataLayout {
                offset: 0,
                bytes_per_row: Some(GPU_ATLAS_EXTENT * 4),
                rows_per_image: Some(GPU_ATLAS_EXTENT),
            },
            wgpu::Extent3d {
                width: GPU_ATLAS_EXTENT,
                height: GPU_ATLAS_EXTENT,
                depth_or_array_layers: GPU_ATLAS_EXTENT,
            },
        );
        self.enabled = true;
    }
}

const _: () = {
    assert!(std::mem::size_of::<SdfBrickPageGpu>() == 48);
    assert!(std::mem::size_of::<SdfSceneGpu>() == 48 + 48 * MAX_SDF_BRICKS);
};
```

### `src/sdf/mod.rs` | **Строк:** 245

```rust
//! SDF foundation: distance-field baking, sparse brick registry, and the
//! CPU cone-tracing reference used by SDF shadows (and later by DDGI in
//! Phase 5).
//!
//! Layout:
//! * [`bake`] — CPU baker producing a 64³ signed distance field per mesh
//!   (`DistanceField64`, [`bake_mesh`]).
//! * [`atlas`] — CPU-side registry mapping mesh ids to placed bricks
//!   ([`SdfBrickAtlas`]).
//! * [`gpu_atlas`] — 128³ GPU atlas + multi-brick page table uploaded for PBR.
//! * [`SdfShadowScene`] — world-space queries over the atlas plus
//!   [`SdfShadowScene::trace_cone`], the ground-truth implementation of the
//!   cone-traced shadow integral. `shaders/sdf_shadow.wgsl` mirrors it
//!   one-to-one for the GPU path.
//!
//! # Cone integral (shared CPU/GPU contract)
//!
//! `trace_cone` sphere-marches the cone axis and accumulates occlusion with
//! the standard SDF-AO / voxel-cone-tracing integral: at distance `t` the
//! cone has radius `r = tan(aperture/2) · t`; the fraction of the cone
//! cross-section blocked by solid at that ring is `saturate(1 - sd/r)`,
//! weighted by the ring's angular coverage `min(1, dt/r)` and combined
//! **multiplicatively** (`vis *= 1 - α`) so overlapping rings do not
//! over-darken. The function returns *transmittance* in `[0, 1]`
//! (1 = fully lit, 0 = fully occluded) — the same quantity
//! `sdf_trace_shadow` in the WGSL module returns.
//!
//! `aperture` is the full cone angle in radians; `aperture → 0` degenerates
//! to a hard binary shadow ray.

pub mod atlas;
pub mod bake;
pub mod gpu_atlas;

pub use atlas::{BrickRef, SdfBrick, SdfBrickAtlas};
pub use bake::{DistanceField64, bake_mesh};
pub use gpu_atlas::{
    GPU_ATLAS_EXTENT, MAX_SDF_BRICKS, SdfBrickPageGpu, SdfGpuAtlas, SdfSceneGpu,
};

use redox_math::Vec3;

/// Hard cap on sphere-marching steps per cone trace.
const MAX_CONE_STEPS: u32 = 128;
/// Occlusion saturation threshold — stop marching once nothing is visible.
const VIS_EPS: f32 = 1.0e-3;

/// Scene-level SDF shadow queries over a brick atlas.
///
/// This is the CPU ground truth for `shaders/sdf_shadow.wgsl` and doubles as
/// the offline validation path (unit tests, future DDGI ray budget checks).
pub struct SdfShadowScene {
    pub atlas: SdfBrickAtlas,
}

impl SdfShadowScene {
    pub fn new() -> Self {
        Self {
            atlas: SdfBrickAtlas::new(),
        }
    }

    /// Smallest texel edge across all bricks (meters); drives the march
    /// step floor. `f32::MAX` for an empty scene (callers return early).
    fn min_texel_size(&self) -> f32 {
        self.atlas
            .iter()
            .map(|b| b.field.texel_world_size().min_element())
            .fold(f32::MAX, f32::min)
    }

    /// Signed distance at world-space `p`, trilinearly sampled from the
    /// brick whose domain contains `p` (the minimum over all containing
    /// bricks when domains overlap). Positions outside every brick report
    /// `f32::MAX` — "far outside any solid" — which the cone integral
    /// treats as unoccluded.
    pub fn sample_world(&self, p: Vec3) -> f32 {
        let mut sd = f32::MAX;
        for brick in self.atlas.iter() {
            if brick.contains(p) {
                sd = sd.min(brick.sample_world(p));
            }
        }
        sd
    }

    /// Cone-traced visibility from `origin` along `dir` (need not be
    /// normalised), returning transmittance in `[0, 1]`.
    ///
    /// See the module docs for the integral. Callers should offset `origin`
    /// off the surface along its normal first (the WGSL entry point does
    /// this internally via its `normal` parameter) to avoid self-shadowing.
    pub fn trace_cone(&self, origin: Vec3, dir: Vec3, aperture: f32, max_dist: f32) -> f32 {
        let dir = dir.normalize_or_zero();
        if dir == Vec3::ZERO || self.atlas.is_empty() {
            return 1.0;
        }
        let t_min = 0.5 * self.min_texel_size();
        let half_tan = (0.5 * aperture).tan();

        let mut visibility = 1.0f32;
        let mut t = t_min;
        for _ in 0..MAX_CONE_STEPS {
            if t >= max_dist {
                break;
            }
            let p = origin + dir * t;
            let sd = self.sample_world(p);
            let r = half_tan * t;

            // Fraction of the cone cross-section blocked at this ring.
            let occ = if r > 1.0e-6 {
                ((r - sd) / r).clamp(0.0, 1.0)
            } else if sd <= 0.0 {
                1.0
            } else {
                0.0
            };

            // Ring-consistent step: fine inside solids, otherwise at most
            // one cone radius per step (never below half a texel).
            let dt = if sd <= 0.0 {
                t_min
            } else {
                sd.abs().clamp(t_min, r.max(t_min))
            };
            // Angular coverage of this ring relative to the whole cone.
            let cov = (dt / r.max(t_min)).min(1.0);

            visibility *= 1.0 - occ * cov;
            if visibility < VIS_EPS {
                break;
            }
            t += dt;
        }
        visibility.clamp(0.0, 1.0)
    }
}

impl Default for SdfShadowScene {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self::new()
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use crate::mesh::primitive::create_cube;

    /// Builds a scene holding one brick: unit cube baked over a 2 m domain
    /// centred at the world origin (cube surface at ±0.5 m).
    fn cube_scene() -> SdfShadowScene {
        let cube = create_cube();
        let field = bake_mesh(&cube, Vec3::splat(2.0));
        let mut scene = SdfShadowScene::new();
        scene.atlas.insert(
            1,
            SdfBrick {
                field,
                origin_ws: Vec3::ZERO,
                world_size: Vec3::splat(2.0),
            },
        );
        scene
    }

    #[test]
    fn cone_trace_visibility() {
        let scene = cube_scene();

        // Origin inside the solid: the very first ring is fully occluded.
        let inside = scene.trace_cone(Vec3::ZERO, Vec3::X, 0.3, 10.0);
        assert!(
            inside < 0.02,
            "cone from inside the solid must be fully occluded, got {inside}"
        );

        // Cone pointing away from the cube: nothing blocks it.
        let away = scene.trace_cone(Vec3::new(2.0, 0.9, 0.0), Vec3::X, 0.3, 10.0);
        assert!(
            away > 0.999,
            "unoccluded cone must transmit fully, got {away}"
        );

        // Grazing cone: axis passes 0.25 m above the top face; the cone
        // radius (tan(0.15)·t) overtakes that clearance only between
        // t ≈ 1.65 and t ≈ 2.8 — partway along the march → partial shadow.
        let grazing = scene.trace_cone(
            Vec3::new(2.0, 0.75, 0.0),
            Vec3::new(-1.0, 0.0, 0.0),
            0.3,
            4.0,
        );
        assert!(
            grazing > 0.1 && grazing < 0.9,
            "grazing cone must be partially occluded, got {grazing}"
        );

        // Directly at the cube face from outside: heavily (but not by
        // definition fully) occluded — must be strictly below full light.
        let at_face = scene.trace_cone(
            Vec3::new(2.0, 0.0, 0.0),
            Vec3::new(-1.0, 0.0, 0.0),
            0.3,
            4.0,
        );
        assert!(
            at_face < 0.5,
            "cone aimed at the cube face should be mostly occluded, got {at_face}"
        );

        // Degenerate aperture (hard ray) at the face: fully blocked.
        let hard = scene.trace_cone(
            Vec3::new(2.0, 0.0, 0.0),
            Vec3::new(-1.0, 0.0, 0.0),
            1.0e-6,
            4.0,
        );
        assert!(
            hard < 0.02,
            "hard ray at the face must be blocked, got {hard}"
        );

        // Empty scene: everything lit.
        assert_eq!(
            SdfShadowScene::new().trace_cone(Vec3::ZERO, Vec3::X, 0.3, 5.0),
            1.0
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn sample_world_matches_field() {
        let scene = cube_scene();
        // 0.25 m outside the +X face → +0.25.
        let sd = scene.sample_world(Vec3::new(0.75, 0.0, 0.0));
        assert!((sd - 0.25).abs() < 1.0e-3, "got {sd}");
        // 0.25 m inside the +X face → -0.25 (trilinear across interior texels).
        let sd = scene.sample_world(Vec3::new(0.25, 0.0, 0.0));
        assert!((sd + 0.25).abs() < 1.0e-3, "got {sd}");
        // Outside the brick domain → "far outside".
        assert_eq!(scene.sample_world(Vec3::new(50.0, 0.0, 0.0)), f32::MAX);
    }
}
```

```rust
//! Shader loading: compile-time [`include_str!`] with optional runtime hot-reload.
//!
//! Every built-in shader lives as a real `.wgsl` file under
//! `crates/redox_render/shaders/` and is embedded into the binary at compile
//! time via the `*_WGSL` constants below — a default build never touches the
//! filesystem for shaders.
//!
//! With the `shader-hot-reload` feature enabled, [`load`] reads the `.wgsl`
//! file from disk at runtime instead, falling back to the embedded copy when
//! the file is missing or unreadable.
//!
//! Note: this module currently only provides the load indirection. A watcher
//! that detects file changes and recreates `wgpu::ShaderModule`s (and the
//! pipelines depending on them) at runtime is planned as follow-up work.

pub const FORWARD_WGSL: &str = include_str!("../../shaders/forward.wgsl");
pub const PBR_WGSL: &str = include_str!("../../shaders/pbr.wgsl");
pub const SHADOW_WGSL: &str = include_str!("../../shaders/shadow.wgsl");

pub const VSM_SHADOW_TEMPORAL_WGSL: &str = include_str!("../../shaders/vsm_shadow_temporal.wgsl");
// Legacy aliases (hot-reload keys unchanged).
pub const SSAO_WGSL: &str = GTAO_WGSL;
pub const SSAO_BLUR_WGSL: &str = GTAO_BLUR_WGSL;
pub const SSAO_UPSAMPLE_WGSL: &str = GTAO_UPSAMPLE_WGSL;

    include_str!("../../shaders/irradiance_convolution.wgsl");

    include_str!("../../shaders/prefilter_convolution.wgsl");

pub const VG_SHADOW_WGSL: &str = include_str!("../../shaders/vg_shadow.wgsl");
pub const VG_CULL_WGSL: &str = include_str!("../../shaders/vg_cull.wgsl");

pub const HIZ_DOWNSAMPLE_WGSL: &str = include_str!("../../shaders/hiz_downsample.wgsl");

pub const VSM_VISIBILITY_WGSL: &str = include_str!("../../shaders/vsm_visibility.wgsl");
pub const SCATTER_LIGHT_WGSL: &str = include_str!("../../shaders/scatter_light.wgsl");
pub const BLOOM_WGSL: &str = include_str!("../../shaders/bloom.wgsl");
pub const CLUSTER_CULL_LIGHTS_WGSL: &str = include_str!("../../shaders/cluster_cull_lights.wgsl");
pub const PARTICLE_SIM_WGSL: &str = include_str!("../../shaders/particle_sim.wgsl");
pub const PARTICLE_BILLBOARD_WGSL: &str = include_str!("../../shaders/particle_billboard.wgsl");
pub const DDGI_TRACE_WGSL: &str = include_str!("../../shaders/ddgi_trace.wgsl");
pub const SMAA_EDGE_WGSL: &str = include_str!("../../shaders/smaa/edge.wgsl");
pub const SMAA_BLEND_WGSL: &str = include_str!("../../shaders/smaa/blend_weights.wgsl");
pub const SMAA_NEIGHBORHOOD_WGSL: &str = include_str!("../../shaders/smaa/neighborhood.wgsl");

/// Compile-time fallback for [`load`], keyed by shader file stem
/// (e.g. `"pbr"` → [`PBR_WGSL`]). Unknown names yield an empty source; wgpu
/// will reject it with a clear label at module creation.
#[cfg_attr(not(feature = "shader-hot-reload"), allow(unused))]
pub fn fallback(name: &str) -> &'static str {
    match name {
        "forward" => FORWARD_WGSL,
        "pbr" => PBR_WGSL,
        "shadow" => SHADOW_WGSL,
        "normal" => NORMAL_WGSL,
        "ssao" => SSAO_WGSL,
        "ssao_blur" => SSAO_BLUR_WGSL,
        "ssao_upsample" => SSAO_UPSAMPLE_WGSL,
        "velocity" => VELOCITY_WGSL,
        "taa" => TAA_WGSL,
        "msaa_resolve" => MSAA_RESOLVE_WGSL,
        "tone_mapping" => TONE_MAPPING_WGSL,
        "equirect_to_cube" => EQUIRECT_TO_CUBE_WGSL,
        "irradiance_convolution" => IRRADIANCE_CONVOLUTION_WGSL,
        "prefilter_convolution" => PREFILTER_CONVOLUTION_WGSL,
        "brdf_lut" => BRDF_LUT_WGSL,
        "debug_lines" => DEBUG_LINES_WGSL,
        "vg" => VG_WGSL,
        "vg_vis" => VG_VIS_WGSL,
        "vg_resolve" => VG_RESOLVE_WGSL,
        "vg_shadow" => VG_SHADOW_WGSL,
        "vg_cull" => VG_CULL_WGSL,
        "hiz_copy" => HIZ_COPY_WGSL,
        "hiz_downsample" => HIZ_DOWNSAMPLE_WGSL,
        "vertex_compressed" => VERTEX_COMPRESSED_WGSL,
        "skybox" => SKYBOX_WGSL,
        "vsm_depth" => VSM_DEPTH_WGSL,
        "vsm_visibility" => VSM_VISIBILITY_WGSL,
        "scatter_light" => SCATTER_LIGHT_WGSL,
        "bloom" => BLOOM_WGSL,
        "cluster_cull_lights" => CLUSTER_CULL_LIGHTS_WGSL,
        "particle_sim" => PARTICLE_SIM_WGSL,
        "particle_billboard" => PARTICLE_BILLBOARD_WGSL,
        "ddgi_trace" => DDGI_TRACE_WGSL,
        "smaa_edge" => SMAA_EDGE_WGSL,
        "smaa_blend" => SMAA_BLEND_WGSL,
        "smaa_neighborhood" => SMAA_NEIGHBORHOOD_WGSL,
        _ => "",
    }
}

/// Directory holding the `.wgsl` sources, relative to the crate manifest.
#[cfg(feature = "shader-hot-reload")]
fn shaders_dir() -> std::path::PathBuf {
    std::path::Path::new(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR")).join("shaders")
}

/// Load a shader by file stem (e.g. `"pbr"`).
///
/// With `shader-hot-reload`: read from `shaders/<name>.wgsl` on disk so an
/// edited shader can be picked up without recompiling; fall back to the
/// embedded copy if the file cannot be read.
///
/// Without the feature: return the embedded copy (zero I/O).
#[cfg(feature = "shader-hot-reload")]
pub fn load(name: &str) -> String {
    let path = shaders_dir().join(format!("{name}.wgsl"));
    std::fs::read_to_string(&path).unwrap_or_else(|_| fallback(name).to_string())
}

/// Load a shader by file stem (see hot-reload variant).
#[cfg(not(feature = "shader-hot-reload"))]
pub fn load(name: &str) -> &'static str {
    fallback(name)
}

/// Creates a `wgpu::ShaderModule` from WGSL source code.
pub fn create_shader_module(
    device: &wgpu::Device,
    label: &str,
    source: &str,
) -> wgpu::ShaderModule {
    device.create_shader_module(wgpu::ShaderModuleDescriptor {
        label: Some(label),
        source: wgpu::ShaderSource::Wgsl(source.into()),
    })
}

/// Prepends shared compressed-vertex decode helpers to a pass shader.
pub fn shader_with_vertex_decode(source: &str) -> String {
    format!("{VERTEX_COMPRESSED_WGSL}\n{source}")
}

/// Creates a shader module with compressed-vertex decode helpers included.
pub fn create_shader_with_vertex_decode(
    device: &wgpu::Device,
    label: &str,
    source: &str,
) -> wgpu::ShaderModule {
    create_shader_module(device, label, &shader_with_vertex_decode(source))
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    fn validate_wgsl(label: &str, source: &str) {
        let module = naga::front::wgsl::parse_str(source).unwrap_or_else(|e| {
            panic!("{label}: parse failed: {e}")
        });
        let mut validator = naga::valid::Validator::new(
            naga::valid::ValidationFlags::all(),
            naga::valid::Capabilities::all(),
        );
        validator.validate(&module).unwrap_or_else(|e| {
            panic!("{label}: validation failed: {e:?}")
        });
    }

    #[test]
    fn all_embedded_shaders_validate() {
        let with_decode = [
            ("pbr", super::PBR_WGSL),
            ("shadow", super::SHADOW_WGSL),
            ("normal", super::NORMAL_WGSL),
            ("vg", super::VG_WGSL),
            ("vg_vis", super::VG_VIS_WGSL),
            ("vg_shadow", super::VG_SHADOW_WGSL),
            ("vsm_depth", super::VSM_DEPTH_WGSL),
        ];
        for (name, src) in with_decode {
            validate_wgsl(name, &super::shader_with_vertex_decode(src));
        }

        let standalone = [
            ("ssao", super::SSAO_WGSL),
            ("ssao_blur", super::SSAO_BLUR_WGSL),
            ("ssao_upsample", super::SSAO_UPSAMPLE_WGSL),
            ("velocity", super::VELOCITY_WGSL),
            ("taa", super::TAA_WGSL),
            ("msaa_resolve", super::MSAA_RESOLVE_WGSL),
            ("tone_mapping", super::TONE_MAPPING_WGSL),
            ("debug_lines", super::DEBUG_LINES_WGSL),
            ("vg_resolve", super::VG_RESOLVE_WGSL),
            ("vg_cull", super::VG_CULL_WGSL),
            ("hiz_copy", super::HIZ_COPY_WGSL),
            ("hiz_downsample", super::HIZ_DOWNSAMPLE_WGSL),
            ("skybox", super::SKYBOX_WGSL),
            ("vsm_visibility", super::VSM_VISIBILITY_WGSL),
            ("scatter_light", super::SCATTER_LIGHT_WGSL),
            ("bloom", super::BLOOM_WGSL),
            ("cluster_cull_lights", super::CLUSTER_CULL_LIGHTS_WGSL),
            ("particle_sim", super::PARTICLE_SIM_WGSL),
            ("particle_billboard", super::PARTICLE_BILLBOARD_WGSL),
            ("ddgi_trace", super::DDGI_TRACE_WGSL),
            ("smaa_edge", super::SMAA_EDGE_WGSL),
            ("smaa_blend", super::SMAA_BLEND_WGSL),
            ("smaa_neighborhood", super::SMAA_NEIGHBORHOOD_WGSL),
        ];
        for (name, src) in standalone {
            validate_wgsl(name, src);
        }
    }
}
```

### `src/shadow/atlas_allocator.rs` | **Строк:** 90

```rust
//! Shadow-atlas tile allocation for point-light cube shadows.
//!
//! The atlas is a single square depth texture divided into a uniform grid of
//! `TILE_PX × TILE_PX` tiles. Each shadow-casting point light consumes **6**
//! consecutive tiles (one cube face each). Allocation priority is nearest-to-
//! camera first; lights that do not fit keep `NO_TILE` and render unshadowed.

/// Edge length of one tile in pixels.
pub const TILE_PX: u32 = 512;
/// Atlas edge length in pixels (must be a multiple of [`TILE_PX`]).
pub const ATLAS_PX: u32 = 8192;
/// Tiles per row/column.
pub const TILES_PER_AXIS: u32 = ATLAS_PX / TILE_PX;
/// Total tile count.
pub const TOTAL_TILES: u32 = TILES_PER_AXIS * TILES_PER_AXIS;
/// Sentinel written into `PointLightGpu::shadow_tile_base` for unshadowed lights.
pub const NO_TILE: u32 = u32::MAX;

/// Maximum simultaneous shadow casters (6 tiles each).
pub const MAX_CASTERS: u32 = TOTAL_TILES / 6;

/// Allocates consecutive 6-tile runs for point-light casters.
#[derive(Debug, Default)]
pub struct ShadowAtlasAllocator {
    next_free: u32,
    /// `(entity_hint, allocated_base)` pairs from the current frame.
    live_allocations: Vec<(u64, u32)>,
}

impl ShadowAtlasAllocator {
    pub fn new() -> Self {
        Self {
            next_free: 0,
            live_allocations: Vec::new(),
        }
    }

    /// Starts a fresh frame: resets the bump pointer.
    ///
    /// Stability heuristic: callers sort casters by distance to camera BEFORE
    /// allocating, so the closest lights win when the atlas saturates. Because
    /// ordering changes smoothly across frames, tiles stay roughly stable.
    pub fn begin_frame(&mut self) {
        self.next_free = 0;
        self.live_allocations.clear();
    }

    /// Allocates a 6-tile run. Returns the base tile index or [`NO_TILE`].
    pub fn allocate(&mut self, entity_hint: u64) -> u32 {
        if self.next_free + 6 > TOTAL_TILES {
            return NO_TILE;
        }
        let base = self.next_free;
        self.next_free += 6;
        self.live_allocations.push((entity_hint, base));
        base
    }

    /// Number of casters currently allocated.
    pub fn allocated_casters(&self) -> u32 {
        self.next_free / 6
    }
}

/// Tile-grid column/row for a tile index.
pub fn tile_grid(tile_index: u32) -> (u32, u32) {
    (tile_index % TILES_PER_AXIS, tile_index / TILES_PER_AXIS)
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn allocates_runs_and_saturates() {
        let mut alloc = ShadowAtlasAllocator::new();
        assert_eq!(alloc.allocate(1), 0);
        assert_eq!(alloc.allocate(2), 6);
        assert_eq!(MAX_CASTERS, 42);
        // Fill to saturation.
        for i in 0..40 {
            let _ = alloc.allocate(10 + i);
        }
        assert_eq!(alloc.allocate(999), NO_TILE);
        alloc.begin_frame();
        assert_eq!(alloc.allocate(5), 0);
        assert_eq!(alloc.allocated_casters(), 1);
    }
}
```
